title: 1991–92 National Hurling League
text:
{{Short description|61st season of the National Hurling League}} {{Use dmy dates|date=April 2022}} {{Infobox GAA League |league = 1991–92 National Hurling League |image = |dates = 20 October 1991 – 10 May 1992 |teams = 32 |team1 = Limerick |captain1 = |manager1 = |titles = 10th |team2 = |captain2 = |manager2 = |one = |two = Antrim |three = Kildare |previous = [[1990–91 National Hurling League|1990–91]] |next = [[1992–93 National Hurling League|1992–93]] }} The '''1991–92 National Hurling League''' was the 61st season of the [[National Hurling League]], the top leagues for [[Inter county|inter-county]] [[hurling]] teams, since its establishment in 1925. The fixtures were announced on 28 November 2006. The season began on 20 October 1991 and concluded on 10 May 1992. ==Division 1== {{Infobox football league season |competition=[[National Hurling League|National Hurling League Division 1]] |season=1991-92 |winners=[[Limerick GAA|Limerick]]
10th National League title

(16 February 1992) |highest scoring=[[Tipperary GAA|Tipperary]] 5-24 - 2-6 [[Down GAA|Down]]
(1 March 1992) |matches= 35 |total goals= |longest wins= |longest unbeaten= |longest winless= |longest losses= |highest attendance= |lowest attendance= |attendance= |average attendance= |prevseason=[[1990-91 National Hurling League|1990-91]] |nextseason=[[1992-93 National Hurling League|1992-93]] |updated=10 February 2017 }} The league saw a major restructuring of the usual four divisions of eight teams. Division 1 was split into Group 1A and Group 1B with each group consisting of six teams. The top two teams in each group qualified for the knock-out stage. [[Offaly GAA|Offaly]] came into the season as defending champions of the [[1990–91 National Hurling League|1990-91 season]]. [[Galway GAA|Galway]], [[Down GAA|Down]], [[Laois GAA|Laois]] and Offaly all entered Division 1 as part of the restructuring. On 12 May 1992, [[Limerick GAA|Limerick]] won the title after a 0-14 to 0-13 win over [[Tipperary GAA|Tipperary]] in the final. It was their 10th league title overall.{{cite web|url=http://www.hoganstand.com/general/leagues/nhlrecords.aspx|title=National Hurling League Results 1925-2009|publisher=Hogan Stand|accessdate=18 April 2011|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100805063526/http://www.hoganstand.com/general/leagues/nhlrecords.aspx|archive-date=2010-08-05|url-status=dead}} [[Laois GAA|Laois]] were relegated from Division 1 after being defeated by [[Dublin GAA|Dublin]] in a relegation play-off. |nextseason=[[1992-93 National Hurling League|1992-93]] |updated=11 February 2017 }} Division 2 remained as a single division consisting of eight teams. The first-placed team at the end of the group stage were deemed champions and secured promotion to Division 1. [[Carlow GAA|Carlow]], [[Roscommon GAA|Roscommon]], [[Westmeath GAA|Westmeath]] and [[Wicklow GAA|Wicklow]] all entered Division 2 as part of the restructuring. On 12 April 1992, [[Antrim GAA|Antrim]] secured the title and promotion after a 3-8 to 0-11 win over [[Meath GAA|Meath]] in round 7 of the group stage.
